pr_title: Add rotation controls to editor selection box corners
pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/12433

Replaces the current simple top-centred rotation control with small rotation controls on the corners of the selection box, same as how other applications have it:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22781491/115982157-900cae80-a5a1-11eb-8d4f-daa38ce92cfc.mp4

Since `SelectionBoxDragHandleButton` was made with having the same appearance and handling logic as the regular drag handler in mind, I've changed the abstraction of the selection box controls to the following:
 - (abstract) `SelectionBoxElement`: contains the base appearance and shared logic of all selection box controls.
   - (sealed) `SelectionBoxButton`: simple implementation of buttons for selection boxes.
   - (abstract) `SelectionBoxDragHandle`: contains simple logic for handling mouse dragging.
     - `SelectionBoxScaleHandle`: a type of drag handle used for scaling selected content.
     - `SelectionBoxRotationHandle`: a type of drag handle used for rotating selected content.
     
Felt kinda overengineered at first but I completely wasn't sure about following the old abstraction, so I've made it more sensible with the new controls.

Few notes:
 - I really didn't want to use the undo/redo icons to represent cornered rotation handles, but I've searched for the usual "two-way curved arrows" on the fontawesome website, and got no results or anything similar (tried 45°-rotated two-way straight arrows but felt weird so I've disregarded it).
 - The current logic of having all handles call `updateRotationHandlesVisibility` was the best I can do, I hoped not to have to query which handle is operated or hovered on every update call, but I've come to a conclusion that it's the simplest way to achieve the intended behaviour.
 - I wasn't really fine with having to expose `HoverGained` and `HoverLost` on the selection box controls, but the alternative way of overriding `ReceivePositionalInputAt` to `handles.Any(h => h.ReceivePositionalInputAt(pos))` doesn't quite hold up when moving mouse from one handle to another immediately (with touchscreen for example), as the composite would still be considered hovered and therefore not call the update rotation visibility state method.

issue_context.title: Have slider rotation dongle overlap the timeline
issue_context.body:
It is somewhat annoying having to move to the middle of the screen just to rotate it.

Screenshots or videos showing encountered issue: https://twitter.com/Momochi85/status/1382761208722432001?s=20

osu!lazer version: 2021.410.0
comments: Willing to take this one, but, is displaying the selection box in front of the timeline the desired direction here? was thinking about moving the rotation button to the opposite side of the box instead, rather than blocking the timeline from display.
You mean dynamically moving it depending on whether it is able to be displayed without being covered?
Yep, and if it can't be displayed on all sides, then move it to the centre of the box.

Just above or below sounds fine, but "all sides or centre" sounds like a really bad user experience.

I'm not sure making it dynamically switch sides is a final step, but if you think you can make it happen with minimal implementation then it sounds like a good starting point, at least to see how it feels.

The primary issue here is that there's not enough breathing space for the playfield (it should have padding equivalent to half a hitcircle size, at least).

The secondary issue is the rotation control is too far away from the edge. Other applications generally bundle the rotation control into the selection box's corners:

![20210416 114023 (Figma)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/114963960-ca42c580-9ea8-11eb-8f77-eb47cc8426d4.gif)

I noticed this also happens on the bottom of the editor, so even if you implement the rotation on the corners, the other options should shift to the top of the selection box
![osu_2021-04-16_13-27-58](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/53081750/115018001-9c18b200-9eb7-11eb-9a49-5d61b91cb15a.png)
@frenzibyte are you still planning to look at this one?
Yeah is my focus now. Adding the ability to rotate from the corners of the selection box sounds better, will give it a try first and see how it goes.

review_comments: I'm a bit weirded out by how this works UX-wise now. Feels unintuitive and worse than before. It's probably because the selection box does not rotate itself and always stays upright, and the drag handle responsible for rotation always stays anchored in the same corner it used to be in. For those two reasons it's really difficult to predict what a drag will do.

Yeah not sure how to improve it on this side without basically looking at rotating the selection box already, I guess if this is not really good to go without rotating then this can be blocked or otherwise.
I'll take a look at making the selection box rotate visually with the content, and see if it's simple to add or too complicated.

As an update, I've looked into it and it isn't really possible to support it perfectly without basically refactoring the entire selection handler scaling and rotation logic to not rely on the current blueprints selection quads and update per-frame, so I'm leaving it as-is for now.

Reading all the intertwined logic you have setup in this (and related) classes makes me sleepy.

Also, it's halfway between being flexible and not. For instance, what if we decide the bottom buttons should only display when the bottom centre drag handle is being hovered?

I don't have a solution in mind; just commenting that this is a pretty convoluted setup.
